office_does: The District Court judge hears misdemeanors, gross misdemeanors and traffic cases in Franklin County, holds preliminary hearings and sets bail.
race_blurb: Nonpartisan: presiding Judge Trinity Orosco, a former defense attorney who started the court's Therapeutic Court, seeks a second term against public defender Michael Nguyen. Nguyen argues bail at first appearances and pledges neutral, efficient courtrooms and cost parity with neighboring courts.

candidates.summary: Public defense attorney with five years in Benton and Franklin County courts, including as the county's preliminary appearance attorney.
highlights: Five years as a public defender; 'hundreds of bail arguments' as preliminary appearance attorney [S1]
Pledges to act as 'a neutral officiant of the law rather than imposing my beliefs from the bench' [S1]
Would focus on rehabilitation through therapeutic courts while requiring accountability [S1]
Wants court costs in line with Benton County and Pasco Municipal courts [S1]

experience.basis: First run for the bench after five years of practice, challenging a sitting judge.

safety.basis: Public-defense formation with heavy bail-hearing practice; pledges a rehabilitation focus through therapeutic courts, paired with accountability.

judicial.basis: Commits to applying the law as a neutral officiant rather than imposing personal beliefs from the bench.

candidates.summary: Presiding judge of Franklin County District Court in her first term, after 14 years as a defense attorney in Tri-Cities-area courts.
highlights: Presiding District Court judge; earlier 14 years of defense practice [S1]
Created the court's Therapeutic Court; plans a Veterans Court track [S1][S2]
Expanded the work crew program as an alternative to jail [S2]
Says she brought more than $1 million in state funding and grants to the county [S1]

experience.basis: Sitting presiding judge running on her first-term record, with long prior trial practice and broad judicial endorsements.

safety.basis: Defense formation; built a therapeutic court and expanded work-crew alternatives to incarceration, framed as accountability plus treatment.
